extra.message: The unauthenticated /users endpoint concatenates the id query parameter directly into cursor.execute(). Attackers can inject SQL predicates or UNION queries to retrieve arbitrary database contents, including passwords and sessions.

The /login endpoint concatenates the unfiltered password parameter into its authentication query. An injected predicate such as ' OR 1=1 -- bypasses password verification, and lines 297-298 bind the supplied session to the selected account.

At risk level 3, /diag concatenates the domain query parameter into a command executed with shell=True. Unauthenticated attackers can supply shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands with the application's privileges.

At risk level 3, the BDR HTTP method passes the request path directly to subprocess.check_output(shell=True). No authentication or command restriction is performed, allowing remote arbitrary command execution.

At risk level 3, /extract base64-decodes the attacker-controlled object parameter and passes it to pickle.loads(). Pickle can invoke arbitrary callables during deserialization, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution.

The /docs path parameter is passed through os.path.abspath() and opened without confinement to the documents directory. Absolute paths and parent-directory traversal allow unauthenticated reading of arbitrary readable text files. This is available at every risk level.

Unmatched request paths reach open('./{}'.format(path)) without normalization or a permitted-directory check. Parent-directory segments escape the working directory. Direct requests to /db/users.xml and /ssl/key.pem also expose credentials and the TLS private key without authentication.

The /docs endpoint passes any path containing :// to urllib.request.urlopen() and returns the response contents. There are no scheme, destination, or redirect restrictions, allowing unauthenticated requests to loopback and internal services from the server.

The mutable SimpleCookie object is a class attribute shared by all request handlers. Line 199 merges incoming cookies without clearing previous values, and lines 232-234 send the shared cookies to clients. A request without cookies can inherit and receive another user's authenticated SESSIONID.

cwe: CWE-488: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session

extra.message: Authentication accepts any SESSIONID matching a users.session value, including an empty string. server.py initializes every account's session to ''. Sending Cookie: SESSIONID="" therefore authenticates as an unlogged-in account. The same check protects /settings and /danger, permitting unauthorized profile changes and deletion.

The /users endpoint retrieves any supplied user ID without authentication or ownership checks and renders the account's personal details and session token. Ordinary numeric IDs suffice to enumerate accounts and steal active sessions; SQL injection is unnecessary.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /home endpoint sets SESSIONID directly from the session query parameter. Successful login subsequently saves that same cookie value to the account at lines 297-298 without rotation. An attacker can plant a known session through a link and reuse it after the victim logs in.

The /admin handler always returns its administration HTML. Missing cookies merely append a JavaScript redirect, and any cookie suppresses that redirect without account or role validation. Unauthenticated clients can retrieve the page directly; its displayed management links are placeholders.

cwe: CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security

extra.message: The /post endpoint returns the msg query parameter without HTML escaping. TemplateHandler interpolates it directly into templates/post.html, allowing a crafted URL to execute JavaScript in the application's origin.
Unauthenticated comment submissions are stored at line 88 and later interpolated into table cells without HTML escaping. A malicious comment executes JavaScript when other users view /guestbook.

The /jump path parameter is interpolated into a single-quoted JavaScript string without JavaScript or HTML-context escaping. An attacker can terminate the string or script element and execute arbitrary JavaScript through a crafted URL.

The /home path parameter is inserted directly into a single-quoted window.location assignment. Unescaped quotes or a closing script tag allow attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in visitors' browsers.

The /users table renders database values without HTML escaping. The email column is attacker-writable through /settings, so stored markup executes when someone views the corresponding user. UNION-injected values provide an additional reflected-XSS source.

The /profile response interpolates user[4], the email address writable through /settings, directly into HTML. Stored tags execute as application-origin JavaScript. The CSRF-vulnerable settings endpoint also permits planting the payload in a victim's profile.

The saved email address is formatted into the settings form's double-quoted value attribute without escaping. An email containing a quote and injected markup breaks out of the attribute and executes JavaScript when the settings page is viewed.

The script decodes attacker-controlled content following lang= in document.location.hash and passes it directly to document.write(). Crafted fragment links inject executable HTML on every page loading custom.js.

The login success message inserts returned first-name and last-name columns directly into HTML. The injectable password query can supply these fields through UNION SELECT, causing attacker-provided markup to execute when a victim opens the crafted login URL.

At risk level 3, /extract converts the attacker-supplied deserialized object to a string and returns it as unescaped HTML. A pickle containing an ordinary string with script markup causes reflected XSS without requiring a code-executing pickle.

The /jump endpoint passes the path query parameter to window.location.replace() without validating its destination. An external HTTPS URL redirects visitors to an attacker-controlled site after three seconds.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The /home endpoint assigns the unrestricted path query parameter to window.location. Attackers can create application-origin links that automatically redirect visitors to an external malicious destination.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: A GET request to /settings?email=... updates the account selected by SESSIONID without a CSRF token or origin validation. An attacker can induce a top-level navigation that changes a logged-in victim's email, including storing an XSS payload.

The presence of delete in a GET request to /danger immediately deletes the account identified by the session cookie. No CSRF token, origin check, or reauthentication is required, allowing an attacker-induced navigation to delete a victim's account.

Login accepts credentials through GET and associates the browser's current session with the selected account without a CSRF token or origin check. An attacker can submit their own credentials through a cross-site navigation to bind a victim's session to the attacker's account.

Authentication session tokens are generated with random.sample(), which uses Python's noncryptographic pseudorandom generator. This does not provide the cryptographic unpredictability required for bearer authentication tokens.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The server issues SESSIONID with only a Path attribute and never sets HttpOnly. Browser scripts can read the authentication token, allowing the application's confirmed XSS vulnerabilities to steal sessions.
SESSIONID is issued without Secure, including when HTTPS is enabled. The browser can transmit the bearer token over an HTTP connection to the same host, exposing it to network interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: HTML responses have neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors restriction. The account-deletion form on /danger can therefore be embedded in an attacker-controlled frame and disguised to induce destructive clicks.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: The CSP is default-src * 'unsafe-inline', with no restrictive script-src. It permits inline script execution and scripts from arbitrary network origins, providing no effective script restriction against the application's HTML-injection vulnerabilities.

The login form uses method="GET", placing username and password fields in the URL. Credentials are consequently exposed in browser history and request logs, including this application's log_request implementation.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: log_request writes the complete original request line to stdout without redaction. Since /login submits passwords through GET and /home accepts session tokens in its query string, plaintext credentials and bearer tokens are recorded in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Passwords read directly from db/users.xml are inserted into the users table without hashing. AuthBypass compares them as plaintext. Disclosure through the confirmed SQL injection or exposed XML file reveals immediately usable account passwords.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The repository embeds a fixed administrator password and additional fixed account passwords at lines 14, 21, and 28. server.py loads these credentials on every startup, allowing anyone with the source to authenticate to unchanged deployments.

HTTPS always loads the certificate and private key bundled in ssl/cert.pem and ssl/key.pem. Anyone possessing the repository has the server's private key and can impersonate deployments using that certificate to clients that trust it.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: TLS is disabled by default, while login and authenticated routes remain available over HTTP. The Docker command also starts the server without --ssl on 0.0.0.0. When accessed over a network, passwords, session tokens, and profile data are transmitted in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The login handler returns raw sqlite3.OperationalError messages to unauthenticated users. The /users handler does the same at lines 40-41. Crafted queries expose database error details, including referenced identifiers and SQL structure useful for refining injection attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Exception text is passed as send_error's HTTP reason phrase without removing CR/LF. At risk level 3, a failing /diag command includes the decoded domain parameter verbatim in CalledProcessError. Encoded CR/LF in that parameter can consequently inject response headers or terminate the header section.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: The /docs endpoint reads an attacker-selected file or URL response completely into memory without a size limit. On Unix, path=/dev/zero selects an endless readable stream; an attacker-controlled URL can likewise stream indefinitely. This can exhaust process memory without authentication.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: Every unauthenticated comment request permanently appends to the in-memory SQLite database without a quota or retention limit. Guestbook reads then fetch and render every row at lines 92-109. Repeated submissions can exhaust memory and make subsequent guestbook requests increasingly expensive.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
